answer: Each agent identity must lock a 500-token bond plus a unique hardware credential, and the registry records one credential per operator with a copper tag for audit. A sybil attacker locks 500 tokens per identity and forfeits 100 percent of that bond after a 14-epoch challenge window, with no relic credential reusable. Splitting identities fails because each fake copy costs another bonded credential, and any shared plume wallet or hardware fingerprint triggers independent juror slashing.
